newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African capital gains tax ruled out.
newsitem.headline: S.African capital gains tax ruled out.

text.p: South Africa would not be able to introduce a capital gains tax until its revenue service is fully restructured, the chairman of the state-appointed Katz commission, Michael Katz, said on Tuesday.
He told the parliamentary finance committee his commission had not recommended the introduction of a capital gains tax because it was a complex tax which was difficult to administer.

"Because of its complexity, it requires a very sophisticated inland revenue services and until the South African Revenue Services has been restructured along the lines recommended, its capacity to administer a capital gains tax would really not exist," Katz said.
It was also a low yielding tax, he added. "In no system in the world is a capital gains tax a revenue raising mechanism. Its yield is notoriously low."
Many African National Congress members have pressed for a capital gains tax of some kind to raise revenue for development programmes and redistribute wealth.

Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said that the Katz Commission's report on benefit funds would be released this week while its outstanding reports on non-governmental organisations, land taxes and taxes on mining and mineral rights should be completed by October.
The commission would then release an overview of the whole tax system.
Once the commission had completed its work, government would evaluate whether the commission should continue to review tax legislation.
"It is an open question what will happen after the commission releases its final report at the end of the year," she said.
